title: Chevening Scholarships Kenya 2027/28
description: UK Government scholarship for future leaders from Kenya to pursue a one-year taught master's degree in the UK.
eligibility: Kenyan citizen; undergraduate degree; at least two years of qualifying work experience; meet Chevening eligibility rules.
benefits: Full financial support for a one-year master's, subject to Chevening terms.
requirements: Eligible citizenship, undergraduate qualification, required work experience, three eligible UK course choices, references and education documents.

title: Reach Oxford Scholarship 2027
description: Oxford undergraduate scholarship for students from low-income countries who cannot study for a degree in their home country.
eligibility: Nationals of eligible low-income countries who receive an Oxford undergraduate offer and meet scholarship criteria.
benefits: Course fees, annual living-cost grant and one return airfare per year.
requirements: Apply for and receive an Oxford undergraduate offer and meet the scholarship's nationality and academic criteria.

title: Oxford Mastercard Foundation AfOx Graduate Scholarships 2027/28
organization: University of Oxford / Mastercard Foundation / AfOx
description: Scholarships for African candidates applying to eligible full-time taught postgraduate courses at Oxford.
eligibility: African citizen ordinarily resident in Africa with an eligible Oxford course offer and demonstrated leadership and service.
benefits: Course fees and a grant for living costs, plus scholar support and development opportunities.
requirements: Submit an eligible Oxford graduate application by the relevant course funding deadline and satisfy scholarship criteria.

title: Oxford Optiver Foundation Scholarships 2027
field: Statistics, Computer Science, Physics, Chemistry, Engineering, Mathematics
description: Scholarships supporting women from eligible low- and middle-income countries studying selected postgraduate science courses at Oxford.
eligibility: Female applicants ordinarily resident in an eligible country applying for an eligible master's course beginning October 2027.
benefits: Full course fees and a grant for living costs, plus mentoring and on-course support.
requirements: Apply for an eligible Oxford master's course and meet course and scholarship criteria.

title: HELB Postgraduate Partial Scholarship 2026/27
description: Kenyan postgraduate scholarship for students enrolled in recognized local public or private universities. The 2026/27 cycle has closed; monitor HELB for the next call.
eligibility: Kenyan student admitted to a master's or PhD programme at a CUE-recognized local university; minimum Second-Class Upper Division.
benefits: Up to KSh 200,000 for Master's and KSh 450,000 for PhD under the 2026/27 call.
requirements: Admission letter, academic qualification, programme eligibility and HELB/HEF application documents.

title: Kenya Government Undergraduate Scholarship — HEF 2026/27
description: Government scholarship support for eligible Kenyan students placed in public universities under the Student-Centred Funding Model.
eligibility: Kenyan citizen placed in a public university by KUCCPS and meeting current HEF/Universities Fund eligibility rules.
benefits: Government scholarship contribution assessed according to financial need.
requirements: Admission letter, KCPE/KCSE details, identity and family information, passport photo and HEF application.

title: Elimu Scholarship Programme — Kenya Secondary School
description: Kenya Ministry of Education programme supporting eligible learners from vulnerable and disadvantaged backgrounds. Intake and dates are announced by the Ministry.
eligibility: Eligible Kenyan learners meeting the current Ministry Elimu Scholarship criteria for the relevant intake.
benefits: Education support package defined in the current Elimu Scholarship call.
requirements: Current Ministry application form, learner and guardian identification, school/admission information and documents in the active call.

title: African Development Bank 2027 Internship — Session 1
field: Agriculture, engineering, economics, finance, ICT, governance, communication and other AfDB job families
description: Competitive internship for African nationals commencing January 2027, with placements at AfDB headquarters, regional and country offices; work may be remote or on-site depending on the hiring unit.
eligibility: African Development Bank member-country national; age 30 or below at commencement; currently enrolled in a master’s programme or within one year of obtaining the degree; English or French proficiency.
benefits: Monthly stipend and medical insurance for eligible interns; visa assistance may be provided where applicable.
requirements: Online application, comprehensive CV, proof of enrolment or degree and any additional documents requested by AfDB.

title: Mo Ibrahim Foundation Leadership Fellowship 2027
organization: Mo Ibrahim Foundation / African Development Bank
field: Development policy, economics, finance, governance, strategy and related fields
description: Selective one-year fellowship at the African Development Bank designed to build the next generation of African leaders through high-level strategic work.
eligibility: African national; master’s degree or equivalent in a relevant discipline; normally under 40, with an extended age limit for women with children; at least seven years of relevant experience and demonstrated leadership.
benefits: Annual stipend, official mission travel and foundation-supported arrangements including medical insurance and other benefits described in the official terms.
requirements: CV with date of birth, nationality, education and experience; academic transcripts; three recommendation letters; online application.

title: Commonwealth Fellowships 2027 — Academic & Professional
organization: Commonwealth Scholarship Commission in the UK
field: Science and technology, health systems, innovation, peace and governance, resilience, access and inclusion
description: New Commonwealth Fellowship Programme with Academic and Professional strands for eligible Commonwealth citizens, including Kenyans, to undertake professional development or academic skills exchange in the UK.
eligibility: Eligible Commonwealth citizen; Professional Fellowships generally target mid-career professionals with five years' relevant experience, while Academic Fellowships target PhD-qualified university staff employed by an eligible Commonwealth university.
benefits: Professional or academic development, UK host placement, knowledge exchange and networking under the relevant fellowship terms.
requirements: Check the individual host programme for its exact eligibility, documents and application route.

title: Commonwealth Foundation Open Grants Call 2026
field: Civil society, advocacy, participation, governance and community development
description: Open grants call supporting eligible Commonwealth civil-society organisations with advocacy projects that contribute to inclusive governance and public participation.
eligibility: Eligible Commonwealth civil-society organisations meeting the Foundation's organisational and project criteria; this is an organisational grant rather than an individual student scholarship.
benefits: Grant funding for approved projects, subject to Commonwealth Foundation terms.
requirements: Eligible organisation, track record of advocacy, clear problem statement, credible project approach and evidence of consultation with intended beneficiaries.

title: Wellcome Career Development Award
description: Funding for mid-career researchers ready to lead a substantial and innovative health-related research programme. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis under the current scheme rules.
eligibility: Mid-career researcher able to lead a substantial innovative research programme and based at an eligible administering organisation under the scheme's location rules.
benefits: Support for an investigator-led research programme; exact award value and duration depend on the approved proposal and scheme terms.
requirements: Strong research track record, substantial innovative programme, eligible administering organisation and required research proposal documents.

title: UNESCO Communication & Information Internship Pool 2026
field: Communication, information, media literacy, digital transformation and related areas
description: UNESCO internship opportunity for students and recent graduates. The Communication and Information Sector internship notice accepts applications for assignments at headquarters, field offices and institutes.
eligibility: At least 20; currently in the third/final year of a bachelor’s, enrolled in a second degree/master’s/PhD, or graduated within the last 12 months; excellent English or French.
benefits: Practical international experience, professional exposure and learning opportunities; UNESCO states that internships are unpaid.
requirements: CV/resume, motivation letter, proof of enrolment or recent diploma and language/technical requirements.

title: UNESCO IITE CIPP Global Youth Innovation Campaign 2026
field: Sustainability, innovation, creative arts, solutions and AI short video
description: Global youth innovation campaign for children and young people to submit creative work or practical solutions around protecting the planet and sustainability.
eligibility: Children and youth categories with age bands; school/partner invitation code is required under the campaign registration process.
benefits: Student awards and recognition for sustainability and innovation work.
requirements: Register an entry, complete participant registration and submit work in an approved category; AI is permitted only in the AI Short Video category.

title: Erasmus+ Youth Exchanges & Youth Participation Activities
field: Youth leadership, civic participation, culture, skills and non-formal learning
funding: Travel, activity and practical-cost support under approved projects
description: Erasmus+ supports youth exchanges and youth participation projects. Individual participation normally occurs through an approved youth organisation or project rather than a single central scholarship application.
eligibility: Youth exchanges generally involve participants aged 13–30; group leaders must be at least 18. Exact eligibility depends on the approved project.
benefits: Supported travel and practical/activity costs under the Erasmus+ funding rules; Youthpass recognition for youth exchanges.
requirements: Join an eligible youth organisation/project and meet the age and project-specific participation requirements.

title: Teach For Kenya Fellowship 2027/2028
field: Education, teaching, leadership and community impact
funding: Fellowship support — see current programme terms
description: Two-year leadership and education fellowship for graduates and young professionals committed to serving in classrooms and communities across Kenya.
eligibility: Teach For Kenya announced the 2027/2028 cohort for graduates and young professionals aged 18–35 who are passionate about education and leadership.
benefits: Classroom experience, leadership development, professional growth and service in Kenyan communities.
requirements: Online application, assessment process and programme-specific selection requirements.

title: NYOTA On-the-Job Experience (OJE) — Kenya Youth
description: NYOTA reopened its On-the-Job Experience window in October 2026 to expand skills training and employment opportunities for vulnerable young Kenyans, including youth with low levels of education.
eligibility: Targeted vulnerable Kenyan youth, with priority including young people with low education levels, refugees and youth facing multiple vulnerabilities; exact intake criteria apply.
benefits: On-the-job experience and employability support under the NYOTA programme.
requirements: Current NYOTA application and eligibility requirements for the reopened OJE window.

title: UNESCO IICBA Community of Practice on Teacher Education Reform
organization: UNESCO IICBA / GPE KIX Africa 19 Hub
field: Teacher education, in-service professional development and education policy
description: Virtual community of practice for education officials, teacher educators, teacher representatives, technical experts and project leaders in Africa to share and learn about teacher development policies and programmes.
eligibility: Education and teacher-development stakeholders in Africa who fit the programme's professional participant profile.
benefits: Virtual workshops, peer learning, discussion and an applied learning task focused on teacher education reform and continuous professional development.
requirements: Professional involvement in teacher education, regulation, teacher development or related education policy work.
